title: Baki Hanma wants YOU to love your muscles
summary: Using Baki's fight with Gaia, who claims Baki abuses his body, NH argues that hard training is the truest form of love for your body. Body and soul are one, muscle growth is a natural adaptation coded into our DNA, and the urge to quit comes from the mind, never the body.
claims: Gaia's idea that hard training abuses the body and that bodybuilding is an ego chase is a demoralisation tactic, and demoralisation is the strongest negative force in the world
Loving your body means pushing it to its limits and giving it fuel to evolve, not treating it like something fragile
The body is not a mount the mind rides and discards; body and soul are two sides of the same coin, so there is no slavery or betrayal between them
As long as you train with adequate severity and give your body time to recover, every workout is the purest form of love for it, and it repays you by growing bigger, stronger and more resilient
Hypertrophy as a response to damage is not unnatural; if muscles were not supposed to grow, that adaptive response would not be coded in our DNA
A built body proves you are actively involved in how you present yourself and that you are willing to work hard
Given how poor average mobility, strength and endurance have become, training should be mandatory, and those who do it show strength of character
The one who wants to sit around is you, not your muscles; they atrophy in revolt if neglected, and a biceps' life mission is to grow
Not training your body is a sign of hatred, not love; it was engineered to handle constant stress
Stop overthinking genetics, unnatural muscles or overtraining and trust your body and supercompensation; you will be surprised how far you get
Your body tells you about tendon pain or running out of breath, but it never tells you to stop training; lack of progress and muscle pain are excuses the mind invents to quit
